html:
The Ngaatjatjarra are an Aboriginal people of the Western Desert, in the ranges east of Warburton in Western Australia, near the borders with the Northern Territory and South Australia. They speak a dialect of the Western Desert language and belong to the Western Desert cultural bloc.

In the 1600s and 1700s, the years the map shows, they lived in small mobile family groups. Water was the key to life in this dry country: people knew every rockhole and soak, and moved between them after rain. Their close relatives are the Ngaanyatjarra and the Pitjantjatjara, whose dialects they can understand.

Contact with outsiders came late, mostly in the 1900s, after a mission opened at Warburton in 1934. Today Ngaatjatjarra people live in communities such as Warakurna, Wanarn, Tjukurla and Patjarr. Their wider history is in Aboriginal Australian societies.
